\chapter{Boys, Girls, Husbands, Wives}
\label{ch:hi-husbands-wives}
\hlchaptermodality{118}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can talk about a boy or a girl, a husband or a wife, and a relative.}

Complete HI-C118-rishtedar: the people in an introduction.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[laṛkā]{\hi{लड़का} (laṛkā) — a boy; a son}

\label{lesson:HI-C118-larka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for a brother's wife, then the Hindi for the in-laws' home.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{लड़का}}
\textbf{\hi{लड़का}} (\emph{laṛkā}) — \textquotedblleft{}a boy\textquotedblright{}, and in a family, \textquotedblleft{}a son\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\hi{बेटा}} is \textquotedblleft{}son\textquotedblright{} as a family word; \textbf{\hi{लड़का}} is any boy.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A boy, beside the word for son you know.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{laṛkā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{laṛkā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{ek laṛkā}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for a brother's wife, then the Hindi for the in-laws' home, then say \emph{laṛkā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{लड़का} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A boy; a son\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[laṛkī]{\hi{लड़की} (laṛkī) — a girl; a daughter}

\label{lesson:HI-C118-larki}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for the in-laws' home, then the Hindi for a boy.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{लड़की}}
\textbf{\hi{लड़की}} (\emph{laṛkī}) — \textquotedblleft{}a girl\textquotedblright{}, and in a family, \textquotedblleft{}a daughter\textquotedblright{}.

The \textbf{-\hi{ई}} ending marks the girl, as in \textbf{\hi{दादी}} beside \textbf{\hi{दादा}}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Boy and girl as a pair.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{laṛkī}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{laṛkī}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{ek laṛkā, ek laṛkī}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for the in-laws' home, then the Hindi for a boy, then say \emph{laṛkī} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{लड़की} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A girl; a daughter\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[pati]{\hi{पति} (pati) — a husband}

\label{lesson:HI-C118-pati}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for a boy, then the Hindi for a girl.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{पति}}
\textbf{\hi{पति}} (\emph{pati}) — \textquotedblleft{}a husband\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\hi{मेरे} \hi{पति}} — \textquotedblleft{}my husband\textquotedblright{}, with the respectful plural \textbf{\hi{मेरे}}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A husband.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pati}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pati}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{mere pati}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for a boy, then the Hindi for a girl, then say \emph{pati} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{पति} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A husband\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[patnī]{\hi{पत्नी} (patnī) — a wife}

\label{lesson:HI-C118-patni}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for a girl, then the Hindi for a husband.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{पत्नी}}
\textbf{\hi{पत्नी}} (\emph{patnī}) — \textquotedblleft{}a wife\textquotedblright{}.

It is built on \textbf{\hi{पति}}, with the \textbf{-\hi{ई}} that marks a woman. \textbf{\hi{मेरी} \hi{पत्नी}} — \textquotedblleft{}my wife\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Husband and wife, one built on the other.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{patnī}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{patnī}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{merī patnī}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for a girl, then the Hindi for a husband, then say \emph{patnī} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{पत्नी} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A wife\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[riśtedār]{\hi{रिश्तेदार} (riśtedār) — a relative}

\label{lesson:HI-C118-rishtedar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for a husband, then the Hindi for a wife.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{रिश्तेदार}}
\textbf{\hi{रिश्तेदार}} (\emph{riśtedār}) — \textquotedblleft{}a relative\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\hi{रिश्ता}} is \textquotedblleft{}a relationship\textquotedblright{}, and \textbf{-\hi{दार}} is \textquotedblleft{}one who has\textquotedblright{}: a relative is one who has a tie to you. \textbf{\hi{वह} \hi{मेरा} \hi{रिश्तेदार} \hi{है}} — \textquotedblleft{}he is my relative\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Boy, girl, husband, wife, relative: the people an introduction reaches for.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{riśtedār}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{riśtedār}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{vah merā riśtedār hai}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for a husband, then the Hindi for a wife, then say \emph{riśtedār} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{रिश्तेदार} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A relative\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
